LESSON: WORD AND SENTENCE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 2
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 1
Topic 1.2: Word and sentence LISTENING

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Word and sentence LISTENING. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How do we form LISTENING formation learner should be able to: sounds as they sing rhymes and recite words?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending
2. recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme
3. appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WORD AND SENTENCE LISTENING
Subject: LITERACY ACTIVITIES · Grade: Grade 2
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Word and sentence LISTENING helps you succeed in LITERACY ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WORD AND SENTENCE LISTENING
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending

What this means
In this part you learn to identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Word and sentence LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme

What this means
In this part you learn to recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Word and sentence LISTENING to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 3: Appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model writing: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Word and sentence LISTENING is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Word and sentence LISTENING”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Word and sentence LISTENING to a partner. (skill: recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme)

Example 3: Write 5 neat sentences using new words from this lesson. (skill: appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Word and sentence LISTENING to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending.
3. Practise this skill: recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme.
4. Practise this skill: appreciate that syllables form  Learners are guided to identify words words listened to (flip chart, boar.
5. Make one local Kenya example of Word and sentence LISTENING from your county, market, farm, or school.
6. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Word and sentence LISTENING: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 2 learner study Word and sentence LISTENING?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How do we form LISTENING formation learner should be able to: sounds as they sing rhymes and recite words?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Word and sentence LISTENING means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: identify the number of syllables poems 2 lessons in a word  Learners play rhyming and blending.
5. Be able to: recognize words with similar games with peers e.g. come up with sounds words that rhyme.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
